This page is the lecture, in class and at home. Each section explains one
idea, then shows its experiment. The page checks every step at once.

**In class, the teacher chooses the way for each experiment,** by the topic
and the time:

- **On the simulator** of the section, here on the page: nothing to
  install, and it works at home too.
- **In the real app** on the teacher's laptop, connected to the smart
  screen (HDMI): follow the steps of **Part A**.
- **In the computer lab:** each student follows the **worksheet (PDF)**,
  Part A in the app and Part B on the simulator, and checks each result
  here.
- **AI prompts:** tap **Copy prompt**, then paste it into an AI assistant
  in another tab.
- **You need:** a search engine, Word, an AI assistant that the university allows, and your phone, or only the simulators of this page. **Never type personal data** into an AI tool.

## Key terms

{{< glossary fact-checking reliable-source personal-data copyright app-permission anonymize plagiarism ai-use-statement >}}

## 9.1 Check a claim in two sources

- A **claim** can be checked: a number, a date, a name, a fact.
- It can come from a message, a website or an AI answer.
- Check it in two **reliable sources** that agree. A source that nobody
  can find is not a source.

![Check a claim in two reliable sources.](images/check-claims.png){width=100%}

{{< sim file="sims/fact-check-lab.html" poster="sims/fact-check-lab.png" title="Fact-Check Lab: Sami's AI draft" height="620" >}}

{{< experiment 1 >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Claims and sources"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="keep it: it sounds sure|ask a friend"}
A text gives a study that no library or search can find. What do you do?
:   remove it

    Why: A source that nobody can find is not a source.

An AI text says "Every nurse is a woman." What is the problem?
:   bias: an unfair idea

    Why: Nurses are men and women: the text repeats an unfair idea.
:::
:::

## 9.2 Share and use safely

- Do not share **personal data** of others (an ID, a phone, a photo).
- A picture from a website has **copyright**: use a free one (**Stock
  Images**) or ask, and add a source line.
- An app gets only the **permissions** that its job needs.

![Share and use safely: a free picture, its source, and only the permissions an app needs.](images/share-safely.png){width=100%}

{{< experiment 2 >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Share safely"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the Internet|allow it"}
Which source line is right for a picture from the website Visit Jordan?
:   Picture: Visit Jordan, visitjordan.com

    Why: It names who and where, so the reader can find it.

A calculator app asks for your location. What do you do?
:   deny it

    Why: A calculator needs no location.
:::
:::

## 9.3 AI: a safe prompt and an honest statement

- Never type personal data into an AI: write a **placeholder** such as
  [name] or [phone].
- When you use AI for your work, say so: an **AI-use statement** names the
  tool, what the AI did, what you changed and how you checked.

![Placeholders keep personal data out of the AI.](images/anonymize.png){width=100%}

{{< sim file="sims/prompt-cleaner.html" poster="sims/prompt-cleaner.png" title="Prompt Cleaner: no personal data in the chat" height="560" >}}

{{< experiment 3 >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Safe and honest"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the AI's name only|nothing"}
What do you write instead of a real phone number in a prompt?
:   [phone]

    Why: A placeholder keeps personal data out of the AI.

What does an AI-use statement name?
:   tool, use, changes, checks

    Why: The tool, what the AI did, what you changed and how you checked.
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Responsible or Not? {.challenge}

At *Sunrise Company* and at the college, six people share, use and make
things online, three of them with AI tools. For each one, choose the best
judgement and action.

{{< sim file="sims/responsible-or-not.html" poster="sims/responsible-or-not.png" title="Responsible or Not? Six people, six cases" kind="game" height="480" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · The six cases (harder)"}
The cases: a screenshot with Sami's phone number; an essay written by AI;
a picture for a report; a salary list with names in an AI chat; a
flashlight app that asks for the contacts. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="share it: the group is small|fine: the AI was free"}
Huda shares a screenshot that shows Sami's phone number. What should she do first?
:   crop out the number

    Why: A phone number is personal data: keep only the part that matters.

Sami hands in an essay that an AI wrote. What is it?
:   plagiarism

    Why: Presenting AI text as your own is not honest.

Huda wants a chart of the salary list with names. What does she do first?
:   remove the names

    Why: Salaries with names are personal data: anonymize them first.
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Check a claim in two reliable sources that agree; remove a source that nobody can find.
- Do not share personal data of others; use free pictures and add a source line.
- An app gets only the permissions that its job needs.
- Never type personal data into an AI: use placeholders such as [name].
- Say how you used AI: the tool, what it did, what you changed and how you checked.
